messages:
Maya H: sev2 page — multiple GPU nodes (infer-prod-us-west-2) are flapping, containers restarting, seeing repeated CUDA OOMs and allocator fragmentation on paged-kv. Noticing slow memory creep over past 12 hours. Can oncall take?
Oncall Bot: Incident created: INC-1765003210 · Sev2 · Channel: #eng-oncall · Command: /ack Maya H
Samir: I'm on it, grabbing allocator traces and dmesg from the affected nodes. Starting with node-qa-03 and node-infer-07.
Cheng Wei: ETA 5m to confirm if it's KV cache fragmentation or a scheduler regression. Can someone check recent rollout? Any new model weights or quantization changes?
Lee: No config rollouts in the last 24h. We did enable a higher max_seq for some customers earlier (route: long-context), not a model change.
Samir: Logs: `E tensorflow: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB` followed by `allocator: paged-alloc: slab split failure, fragment>threshold` and repeated `kvcache: page_resident_count spike`.
Priya: Customer impact: a subset of requests are 500'ing (~3% for realtime route), retrying causes extra load. We've got a support ticket (SUP-9872) started.
Cheng Wei: Quick mitigation options: 1) cordon + drain hottest nodes, 2) roll back long-context autoscaling, 3) reduce batch size or set KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD lower. What's safest?
Maya H: Start with cordon/drain for the worst nodes to stop churn. Then apply a temporary qflag to reduce batch_size to 1 for affected pools. If that reduces pressure, we can look at eviction thresholds.
Samir: Executing: `kubectl cordon node-infer-07 && kubectl drain node-infer-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
Ops Bot: node-infer-07 cordoned and drain job started by Samir. Pod restarts will be observed in ~30s.
Samir: After drain, crash rate dropped but memory on node-infer-09 still climbing slowly. I pushed `export REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.45` to the runtime env on the pool (hotfix) and restarted runtime. Observing immediate drop in resident set.
Cheng Wei: Good. Can we also enable prefix/KV caching diagnostic mode to gather page-level fragmentation stats? Add `--kv-debug=pages` for 1h and upload traces to /tmp/kvdump-1765003210.tgz
Lee: Doing `kubectl set env deploy/infer-runtime REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=pages --namespace=prod` and `kubectl rollout restart deploy/infer-runtime` on a single AZ.
Priya: Noting customer-facing triage: CS notified customers in SUP-9872 that degraded tail latencies and occasional 500s are being mitigated, ETA for stable baseline ~1h.
Maya H: If this recurs after drain+evict tweak, fallback plan: route affected traffic to a smaller model variant (v1-small) via smart routing policy to reduce KV pressure. Prep checklist for that switch?
Samir: Routing switch ready, can flip weighted routing in the control plane and ramp in 10% increments. Will coordinate with Maya.
Cheng Wei: Uploading kv dump now. Preliminary looks show high page count with lots of subpage fragmentation; fragmentation ratio ~0.62 and slowly increasing. Suspect a leak combined with paged-attention growth for long-context requests.
Oncall Bot: Update: INC-1765003210 · node-infer-07 drain succeeded · node-infer-09 memory stabilized after env tweak.
Lee: Monitoring for 20m. If stable, uncordon remaining capacity and keep `REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.45` as temporary default.
Priya: CS updated customers: mitigation in place, partial traffic reroute if we see reoccurrence. No major outages, degraded error rate reduced to ~0.5%.
Maya H: Post-incident actions: 1) create follow-up eval to reproduce long-context sequence allocations, 2) add sampling for paged-kv fragmentation to datadog dashboards, 3) plan for an allocator defrag pass / compaction job. Assigning to Cheng and Samir.
Samir: Ack, will open a ticket with reproducer and add regression test to nightly.
Cheng Wei: Will draft a safe compaction plan (offline compaction pass with throttled IO) and propose a gradual rollout.
Maya H: Thanks team — keeping incident open until 3h clean window. If no regressions, we'll close and move to postmortem. :thumbsup:
Ops Bot: Incident INC-1765003210 annotated: mitigation steps recorded.
